learning_objective: 🎯 Discover who owns the businesses around us! Learn the differences between private companies, government-owned enterprises, and massive multinational corporations.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Private sector businesses are owned by individuals (like Reliance or Tata) to make profits. Public sector businesses are owned and managed by the government (like Indian Railways or LIC) to provide services and ensure public welfare.

1. Departmental Undertakings (run as a government ministry, e.g., Railways, Post Office). 2. Statutory Corporations (created by a special act of parliament, e.g., LIC, RBI). 3. Government Companies (where the govt holds at least 51% shares, e.g., BHEL, SAIL).
Huge corporations that have their headquarters in one country but operate in several other countries (e.g., Coca-Cola, Samsung). They bring foreign capital, advanced technology, and mass employment.
A model where the government and a private sector company collaborate to finance, build, and operate projects like highways, airports, or hospitals.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Logo Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Look at the products in your home. The soap might be from Unilever (MNC). The electricity might come from a State Electricity Board (Statutory Corporation). The train ticket you booked is Indian Railways (Departmental Undertaking). You are surrounded by all three sectors every day!

exam_tips: 📌 A Government Company is defined as one where at least 51% of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central or State government.
📌 Statutory Corporations have financial autonomy; they do not get their budget directly from the government treasury like Departmental Undertakings do.
📌 MNCs are characterized by huge capital resources, advanced technology, and centralized control (headquarters).
quick_recap: ⭐ Departmental undertakings lack flexibility and suffer from red tape and political interference.
⭐ Joint Ventures allow two companies to pool their resources, share risks, and access new markets.
⭐ The role of the public sector in India was redefined after the 1991 economic reforms, leading to privatization and disinvestment.
